extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs, Department of the Interior officials, and United States Indian agents
extracted.subtask_description: Annual-report style policy and operational recommendations for managing Indian agencies (reservation selection, buildings, schools, supplies, policing, and treatment of Indians) as addressed to the Commissioner of Indian Affairs and Department officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disarmament and safekeeping of Indian arms
rubrics_metrics.description: When Indians are to be disarmed they should be allowed to surrender their guns and horses to the agent, who will give each a receipt for their guns and return them after the present troubles were over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent argued that Indians, relying on him as their friend, would not have come in if they had known of forcible disarmament; deception or surprise disarmament causes flight, confusion, and may produce skirmishes. Avoid letting military 'turn their Indians loose' (scouts) who may then attack others; allow surrender to a trustworthy agent with receipts rather than unexpected military seizures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane handling and sanitary custody of detained Indians
rubrics_metrics.description: If Indians are placed under guard or corralled they must not be confined in unhealthy, filthy enclosures where old manure is several inches deep, creating sickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When hurried removals and military searches occur, Indians may lose valuable non-contraband property and animals; authorities should avoid unnecessary confiscation, provide sanitary corrals (avoid deep manure), and take steps to prevent sickness. The report cites >200 horses sent to Fort Stanton with only 42 remaining due to death, killing, or claims—indicating need for better care and accounting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability and promptitude of contractors supplying agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Contractors, both of supplies and freight, should be held to strict account for promptitude in the forwarding and delivery of goods and supplies at the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure of contractors to deliver flour and corn in spring caused distress and near-starvation among aged and infirm Indians; where contractors fail, the department should make open-market purchases but should also enforce contracts and hold contractors strictly accountable for timely delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency buildings must be habitable and appropriately sited
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency buildings (storehouse, agent's residence, corrals) should be made habitable, sound, and located in healthy localities; appropriation should be made for new buildings where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report documents rotten slab construction, leaking roofs, flooded rooms, vermin, snakes, and decayed adobe foundations. Recommends removal of the agency about one mile east to a healthier site and Congressional appropriation for new buildings; corral foundations must be rebuilt to avoid danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irrigation and water infrastructure to reduce nomadism
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement irrigation (wind-engines, stock pumps) across the reservation to provide water for herds and farming, thereby keeping many Indians within reservation limits and lessening nomadic movements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes 30 wind-engines and 52 stock pumps funded ($3,500) as a means to retain population and improve agriculture; such infrastructure is a recommended investment to make reservations self-sustaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: School infrastructure and educational provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Build and properly equip school-houses (day and boarding) with lodging for teachers; industrial or boarding schools should be provided where suitable, and teacher residences constructed so schools can be graded and made efficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A boarding school building planned to accommodate 150–200 pupils; day schools expanded with furniture and graded instruction increased attendance. Parents may be reluctant to send children to distant boarding schools; agent recommends sending at least two boys and two girls from each pueblo to Carlisle as a start; school success measured by months taught, attendance, and condition of school buildings and furniture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for reservations (winter conditions and size)
rubrics_metrics.description: When selecting reservations consider winter severity (depth of snow) and provide sufficient length (about forty miles) so that portions of the reservation (south end) are out of the snowy district to serve as winter range for horses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report describes a selected reservation as 'very suitable in most respects' except snow depth and recommends making the reservation as long as it ought to be (forty miles) so the south end will be out of the snow—practical criterion balancing summer/winter ranges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize Indian police with adequate compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts to organize a police force among Indians should continue, but compensation offered must be acceptable for Indians to enlist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent reports inability to organize a police force because Indians are unwilling to accept the compensation offered; recommends continuing efforts and adjusting compensation to recruit stable policing among Indians.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisive measures to stop whisky traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt decisive and prompt measures by the government to stop the whisky trade to Indians, which is illegal and an incentive to crime and impoverishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whisky is sold openly by traders at points 40–100 miles from the reservation, often via 'middle men' who stash liquor for Indians. Chiefs uniformly deprecated the traffic and requested federal intervention—action should be taken to enforce the law and suppress dealers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation and restitution for seized or lost Indian property
rubrics_metrics.description: Where property (horses, goods) is seized, corralled, or otherwise lost during military operations or removals, Indians should be accounted for and compensated; promises made (e.g., return of animals) must be honored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agent protested that in hurried removals and soldier searches Indians 'lost much that was valuable to them and not contraband' and that horses sent to Fort Stanton largely disappeared; prisons/removals should not strip faithful Indians nor hold them indefinitely without justification or compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reservation annuity funds to clear title clouds and enable partition
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider using a portion of Indian annuity funds to extinguish external claims (e.g., pre-emption claims) that cloud titles and prevent partitioning lands in severalty, since partition has proved to promote industry and prosperity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report cites Ogden Land Company pre-emption claim impeding Allegany and Cattaraugus partitions; examples (Oneidas, Cornplanter, Tuscaroras) show partitioning lands in severalty fosters farming, industry, and prosperity. Department should protect tribal titles to encourage improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure school performance with attendance and instructional months
rubrics_metrics.description: Report school statistics including number of schools, average months taught, number of children of school age, number attending (any portion and one month+), average daily attendance, and cost/valuation of schoolhouses and apparatus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The New York agency reports 31 schools taught an average of 8½ months, 1,471 children of school age, 1,231 attending some portion, 929 attending one month or more, average daily attendance 733, and financial details of maintenance and contributions—these are the metrics to evaluate school programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural emergency support and seed provision
rubrics_metrics.description: In times of crop failure or drought provide seed (wheat and corn) and emergency purchases to avert starvation and support planting; hold contractors accountable to avoid such crises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Laguna pueblos were reduced to want and received $500 in seed; open-market purchases in June–July relieved hunger. Agencies should intervene early to supply seed and prevent trading away livestock for seed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservoir construction for community water supply
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage and assist construction of reservoirs (e.g., solid masonry wall across creek openings) to store water sufficient for a larger population and improve agriculture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent suggests building a reservoir at Pescado Creek by masonry abutments in a rainbow shape at cost ~$500–$700 to support greater population and enable irrigation—practical local infrastructure recommendation.
